title: Surge remediation chronicle: reservation sculpting & burst-policy hardening
creator: Ava Chen
description: Post-incident action item ticket capturing the investigation and remediation steps for a dedicated-cluster capacity event on 2025-03-01. Incident characteristics: a multi-tenant GPU pool experienced an asymmetric surge driven by a small set of tenants that caused reservation saturation, cascading KV cache evictions, and elevated tail latency for P99 requests. This ticket documents the proposed reservation-sculpting algorithm, burst policy hardening, detection signals, and follow-up tests + rollout plan.
incident_timeline: 2025-03-01 02:58 UTC - Alerts: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-a' P95 token latency increased by 4x; cost burn rose sharply
2025-03-01 03:12 UTC - Autoscaler triggered additional nodes but reservation accounting lagged; retries and eviction spikes observed
2025-03-01 03:22 UTC - Initial mitigation: soft-throttle on noisy tenant group applied via ad-hoc quota; partial recovery observed
2025-03-01 04:05 UTC - Root-cause signals collected: tenant fingerprinting showed 3 tenants with oscillating KV working set; burst tokens depleted rapidly
2025-03-01 06:30 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; postmortem data capture started (trace snapshots, KV hit/miss histograms, scheduler traces)
action_items: Implement reservation-sculpting that decays ephemeral burst credits over epoch windows (prototype: epoch=10m; decay=0.25 per epoch)
Add 'burst-token-leak' detector: 3 consecutive epochs of negative reserve delta -> mark tenant as noisy and move to probation lane
Expose KV cache tunables per-tenant (max_kv_items, eviction_margin) and a hard cap that prevents full-cache thrashing across tenants
Introduce lightweight tenant fingerprinting metric (LRU signature + hot-key skewness) to the telemetry pipeline and dashboard
Create synthetic tenant load generator (tenant-fuzzer) to reproduce the oscillation pattern seen in the incident; include deterministic seeds for regression tests
Ship a canary rollout for burst-policy changes (5% of dedicated pools) with automated rollback on P99 latency > baseline +15%
Document emergency operator runbook for rapid soft-quarantine and reservation rewind with 5 commands and required telemetry checks
Schedule wide-run chaos / soak test against dedicated pools in staging using tenant-fuzzer before production rollout
decisions: Adopt epoch-based decay over instantaneous token drains to avoid cliff-edge failures; tradeoff: slightly longer recovery for noisy tenant vs fewer false positives
Favor soft-quarantine + probation lane rather than immediate hard ejection to preserve customer availability and debugability
KV cache per-tenant soft caps will be user-configurable for Dedicated customers, but default hard caps will be enforced by platform to protect cluster stability
Telemetry-first approach: prioritize visibility (LRU signature, reserve-delta histograms) before complex automated eviction heuristics
tradeoffs: Short epoch (1m) gives faster containment but may cause oscillation; chosen epoch=10m balances responsiveness and stability
Hard caps reduce tail risk but can increase per-request cold starts for heavy tenants; will mitigate via prewarmed cache hints and recommended tenant-sizing docs
Automated ejection simplifies ops but risks customer impact; plan uses probation + human-in-the-loop escalation for first 30 days

2025-03-05 - Tenant-fuzzer v0.1 landed in staging harness: github.com/redwood-inference/tenant-fuzz; scenario 'oscillate-hotset-3' reproduces KV churn at ~95% fidelity
2025-03-06 - Dashboard widgets added to Console: 'Tenant reserve-delta', 'LRU signature entropy' (console PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2143)
2025-03-09 - Internal RFC posted summarizing algorithm and rollout plan: confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Reservation+Sculpting+RFC
2025-03-10 - Canary job scheduled for 2025-03-12 on eu-west-2-a (5% nodes); alert thresholds and rollback playbook authored
acceptance_criteria: Canary run (5% nodes) shows no P99 regression > 10% compared to baseline across 72h
Tenant-fuzzer reproduces incident pattern deterministically in staging and is added to CI nightly (stability-run stage)
KV cache hard caps prevent cross-tenant eviction storms in synthetic test with 50 concurrent tenants
Runbook reviewed and approved by SRE, Product, and Solutions Engineering
Telemetry shows reserve-delta, LRU entropy, and burst-token histograms available in 1-minute resolution
notes: Follow-on: consider short-circuit hot-key detection to proactively recommend model quantization or smaller batch sizes to tenants that cause thrash
Customer comms: for affected customers, Solutions Eng to deliver one-on-one incident email summarizing mitigations and recommended tenant sizing
Long-term: evaluate ML-based noisy-tenant classifier using LRU entropy + request signature embeddings (tracked in project 'noisy-tenant-detection')
